quote: async def embed(self, text: str) -> list[float]:
why: The base contract gains an abstract async embed(text) -> list[float] (base.py:68-84). All three concrete clients implement it: OpenAIClient.embed (providers/openai.py:78), CircuitBreakerLLMClient.embed (wrapper.py:97), ScriptedLLMClient.embed (tests/eval/fakes.py:96). Measured: pytest -k embed -v across the three touched test files -> 8 passed, so the abstract contract is satisfied and every client is instantiable.

embed() awaits AsyncOpenAI.embeddings.create(...) - the SDK call that issues POST {base_url}/embeddings. test_embed_calls_configured_model_and_dimensions patches exactly that method and asserts model=custom-embed-v2, input=hello world, dimensions=8: non-default witness values, so a hardcoded model or dimension would fail the test.

Every element is float()-coerced and the length is checked against the configured dimension before returning; a mismatch raises ValueError naming expected and actual (openai.py:97-102). test_embed_returns_list_of_floats feeds ints 1,2 and asserts [1.0,2.0] with every element float; test_embed_rejects_vector_with_wrong_dimensions configures 3, returns 2 and asserts the ValueError. Both pass.

embedding_model (line 71, default text-embedding-3-small) and embedding_dimensions (line 75, default 1536, ge=1) are LLMSettings fields under the LLM_ env prefix. OpenAIClient.__init__ accepts both and from_settings forwards them (openai.py:71-72); .env.example documents LLM_EMBEDDING_MODEL and LLM_EMBEDDING_DIMENSIONS. Tests pin defaults, env overrides, the from_settings forwarding and the wire call (8 embed tests pass). Flat fields are the issue's permitted option when a separate EmbeddingConfig is unnecessary.

The issue's path tests/llm/test_client.py does not exist; the repo mirrors src/ under tests/, so the suite is tests/unit/test_llm.py and the issue text is stale. Measured at 845a92a from /tmp with LLM_API_KEY and LLM_EMBEDDING_* unset (no .env available): pytest tests/unit/test_llm.py tests/unit/test_factory_breaker.py tests/config/test_models.py -q -> 76 passed. Full suite in the repo: pytest -q -> 1308 passed, 32 skipped, 0 failed. The 8 new embed tests pass and no new test depends on a developer .env (all LLMSettings are built with _env_file=None).

The two new fields land in the config slice src/cortex/config/llm.py; the hunk adds no import (the module imports pydantic, pydantic_settings and cortex.config.base), so the documented seam is respected: cortex/llm/config.py says the settings slice moved to cortex.config.llm precisely so the config layer does not import the cortex.llm package, whose __init__ eagerly loads the OpenAI SDK. The pre-existing TYPE_CHECKING-only import of cortex.llm.models is untouched and loads nothing at runtime. cortex.llm.config still re-exports LLMSettings unchanged. Measured: ruff check on the 8 touched Python files -> All checks passed (pyproject select E,F,I,N,W,UP).

quote: ADR-0008: embeddings are generated eagerly at fact-storage time through
why: ADR-0008 decides eager embedding generation through the provider embedding endpoint (text-embedding-3-small) via LLMClient.embed(), with caller-side ILIKE fallback. The implementation matches: defaults text-embedding-3-small/1536, the OpenAI /embeddings endpoint, and provider errors re-raised unchanged for the #31 fallback. store_fact() wiring and the pgvector column are outside this ticket's stated boundaries (No Postgres changes yet / No fact storage changes yet), so their absence is not a deviation.

embed follows the established contract: abstract async method on LLMClient like chat/chat_stream, a concrete provider implementation with the same log-and-reraise APIError idiom as chat (openai.py:168-170), and an explicit pass-through in CircuitBreakerLLMClient. Only chat is routed through the breaker; chat_stream already bypasses it with a recorded reason (wrapper.py:81-87), and embed does the same with the reason in its docstring - an embedding outage must not open the breaker gating chat (issue #30 decision 6). test_embed_delegates_directly_without_breaker asserts the delegation and that breaker.call is not awaited; it passes.
